name: Block Operational Technology Message
summary: Adversaries may block messages between systems and devices in an OT/ICS environment to disrupt processes. Messages typically fall into two categories: (1) reporting messages that contain telemetry data about the current state of systems, devices, and processes and (2) command messages that contain instructions to control systems, devices, and processes. Both types of messages are critical for the proper functioning of industrial control…

strategies.name: Detection of Block Operational Technology Message

analytics.name: Analytic 2046
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies iptables/nftables rule changes on Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux gateways that selectively block one ICS communication traffic type. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

analytics.name: Analytic 2213
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an abrupt cessation of expected Industrial Control System (ICS) protocol traffic between a Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA)/control server and a field device, without a corresponding device alarm or scheduled maintenance event, while the device remains reachable for at least some traffic types. This technique-level analytic synthesizes Command Message blocking (T1691.001) and Reporting Message blocking (T1691.002).
